articles.summary: Patrick Stewart, as Captain Jean-Luc Picard. (CBS) The great British actor Sir Patrick Stewart passed away on Thursday . While Stewart began his career as a stage actor and performed in many Shakespeare plays, he is best known for his portrayal of Captain Jean-Luc Picard, in Star Trek: The Next Generation . Thanks to his impressive performance, Stewart and the character he played became science fiction icons. Stewart brought extraordinary depth and perception to the role. And the character is an interesting contrast to the more instinctive and aggressive, less cerebral, Captain Kirk in the original Star Trek Series . Perhaps more than any other character, Stewart's Picard epitomized Star Trek's progressive liberal values: Enlightenment rationalism, technological optimism (highlighted by his defense of the rights of the android Data ), racial and ethnic equality, and commitment to peace and diplomacy. In many ways, Picard and TNG promoted these ideas to an even greater extent than the original series. Whereas Captain Kirk was often belligerent and acted on instinct, Picard sought diplomatic solutions to conflict, and tried to avoid doing anything drastic without careful deliberation

articles.title: Democrats can do something about energy prices — without winning the midterms
articles.author: Eric Levitz
articles.summary: A great deal is at stake in next week’s midterm elections. The partisan makeup of the new Congress will shape future spending bills, congressional investigations, and judicial nominations, among other things. And yet, the most consequential bill of the next 12 months — and the one that speaks most directly to voters’ concerns about the cost-of-living — might well pass before the new Congress is seated. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA) could dramatically reshape America’s energy system. And the bill’s supporters plan to pass it during the House and Senate’s lame-duck session — the months between next week’s elections and the new Congress’s arrival. The bill is long and complex, revising the rules governing everything from how ocean-powered turbines are licensed to what some geothermal plants must pay in royalties . That said, the legislation’s fundamental aim is simple: to make building all forms of energy infrastructure easier. The BAAJA has united fossil fuel companies and green energy firms in its favor — while cleaving the climate movement in two.
